# Examples

The pieces that ship with Cell studio, one plain-text file each in `examples/*.cells` (77 of them): first the tutorial, 39 pieces in 9 tiers, then the pieces, grouped by their first genre tag and listed in the library's order. Open one from the title in the header ([ui/library.md](ui/library.md)).

<!-- Generated by tools/examples-doc.ts from examples/*.cells: run `npm run docs:examples`, do not edit. A test fails when it is out of date. -->

## Tutorial

A tier is a stretch of the language; its pieces together show all of what it introduces and use nothing from a later tier. The numbers of the tiers are stable: a piece added to a tier changes none ([display.md](language/display.md#the-tutorial-tier)).

### Tier 1 · Steps and sound

Introduces a voice and the sound card; steps: numbers, rests, holds, repeats, a rate; notes on the cells.

| piece | file | about | postgain | length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| An oscillator | [`oscillator`](../examples/oscillator.cells) | The smallest piece that sounds: one cell turning its braid 440 times a second, held, heard through the built-in card. | .8 |  |
| A tone: one note, one voice | [`tone`](../examples/tone.cells) | The smallest piece that sounds: a note every second, played by a sine on A4. | 2 | 0:01 loop |
| Rests, holds and repeats: a rhythm on one note | [`rests`](../examples/rests.cells) | One note, played as a rhythm: some steps rest, some are held, some are played twice. | 2 | 0:04 loop |
| Semitones: a scale up and down | [`semitones`](../examples/semitones.cells) | A number is a note: so many semitones above the voice's own. Up the C major scale and back. | 2 | 0:03 loop |
| Two voices: a mix | [`twovoices`](../examples/twovoices.cells) | One tune, played by two voices at once: a sine on top and a saw three octaves below it, quieter. | 2 | 0:05 loop |
| Steps: a tune on one line | [`steps`](../examples/steps.cells) | Frère Jacques written as steps: numbers, rests, holds and repeats, four steps a second. | 2 | 0:11 loop |

### Tier 2 · Time and voice

Introduces a clock: a bar, step=&bar, /2 and *2, a tempo marking; a voice: a source and an envelope; filters and effects, a vibrato.

| piece | file | about | postgain | length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A clock: one bar drives every part | [`clock`](../examples/clock.cells) | A bar sets the tempo, and every part steps with it: on the beat, twice as fast, or once every two beats. | 1.41 | 0:10 loop |
| A voice: a source and an envelope | [`voice`](../examples/voice.cells) | Four voices, each a source and an envelope: a pluck, a swell, a bass and a breath. | 6.31 | 0:04 loop |
| Filters and effects: shaping a voice | [`effects`](../examples/effects.cells) | What shapes a voice after its source: filters, a reverb and an echo, grit, and a vibrato. | 1.68 | 0:04 loop |

### Tier 3 · Melody and harmony

Introduces tables: over=, scale(), shift=; show= and size=; motifs: splicing, reuse, degrees (^n); chords and a progression: accidentals, a sum of pitches.

| piece | file | about | postgain | length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Key and mode: one theme, two wheels | [`transpose`](../examples/transpose.cells) | One theme, read through a mode and a key. | 2.11 | 0:05 loop |
| Motifs and reuse: Twinkle Twinkle | [`twinkle`](../examples/twinkle.cells) | Twinkle Twinkle from three motifs, one of them read a step up the scale, in solfège. | 1.58 | 0:30 loop |
| Chords and a progression | [`chords`](../examples/chords.cells) | Four chords in A minor, struck on the beat, and the bass that follows them. | 2.99 | 0:10 loop |

### Tier 4 · Rhythm and feel

Introduces meter and feel: a bent bar, gates; drums: a groove of voices, ratchets, a subsequence, euclid, a kit; swing: a swing clock, swing= and beat=.

| piece | file | about | postgain | length |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Drums: a groove of voices | [`drums`](../examples/drums.cells) | A drum part written with the drums' names: a beat, a fill with ratchets and a subsequence, a Euclidean rhythm and a kit. | .944 | 0:08 loop |
| Swing: the long and the short | [`swing`](../examples/swing.cells) | Eighths played long and short: a swing clock, and the same feel from swing= on the bar. | 1.88 | 0:04 loop |

### Tier 5 · Development

Introduces canon: a theme shifted; mirrors: retrograde, slices, picks, transposing, inverse(); variations: a copy changed where it says (base=, =); chance and choice; turning tables: stride=, cycle(&x), the circle of fifths; arrangement: parts as taps of the bar, a selector, laps=, off.

| piece | file | about | postgain | length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Canon: Frère Jacques | [`canon`](../examples/canon.cells) | Frère Jacques as a round: four voices, each a bar behind the last. | 1.33 | 0:16 loop |
| Mirrors: backwards, upside down, in pieces | [`mirrors`](../examples/mirrors.cells) | One motif heard forwards, backwards, higher, upside down, and taken apart. | 4.22 | 0:13 loop |
| Variations: a subject and its copies | [`variations`](../examples/variations.cells) | One subject entered three times, as a fugue begins: as it is, a fifth up with its leap bent (a tonal answer), and an octave down with its last note held. Each entry after the first is a copy of the subject, written as what changes. | 3.98 | 0:08 loop |
| Chance and choice | [`chance`](../examples/chance.cells) | A line that is never quite the same twice round: steps that may not sound, and choices between notes. | 1.58 | 0:02 loop |
| A table that turns: the circle of fifths | [`fifths`](../examples/fifths.cells) | A key that turns a fifth each pass: round the circle of fifths and home. | 2.37 | 0:52 loop |
| Arrangement: parts and a song | [`arrangement`](../examples/arrangement.cells) | Three parts, and a song that picks which of them play: an intro, a verse, a chorus, an end. | 2 | 0:34 |

### Tier 6 · Sound and tuning

Introduces stereo: pan=; waveforms from braids: audio rates, sin(), ramps, tables, an instrument; moving parameters: a filter that opens, a fade in decibels; tuning: grids; free(): sliders and named choices; meter().

| piece | file | about | postgain | length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stereo: Mary Had a Little Lamb | [`stereo`](../examples/stereo.cells) | Mary Had a Little Lamb across two channels: the bell on the left, the cello on the right. | 1.19 | 0:05 loop |
| Sound: voices, waveforms, envelopes | [`waveforms`](../examples/waveforms.cells) | Voices made of braids: square, triangle, saw and sine, with envelopes and a vibrato. | 1.06 | 0:10 loop |
| Moving parameters: a filter that opens | [`moving`](../examples/moving.cells) | A bass line whose filter opens on every note and swells over four bars, with accents and a fade. | 6.31 | 0:08 loop |
| Tuning: three grids | [`grids`](../examples/grids.cells) | One tune on three grids in turn: nineteen equal steps to the octave, a pure fifth cut in seven, and pure ratios. | 6.31 | 0:16 loop |
| Metronome: any meter | [`metronome`](../examples/metronome.cells) | A bar and the clicks it plays, in a meter you choose. | 1.58 | 0:02 loop |

Introduces FM; a motor; a belt; a resonator; resonators that answer: coupled, excited; a scope.

|---|---|---|---|---|

Introduces a tape; a sound tape: worn, wandering heads; text: spell(); clock time and a law.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Echo Tape | [`echotape`](../examples/echotape.cells) | A tape loop of notes: a write head records the tune and read heads play it back, echoing. | 7.08 | 0:11 loop |
| Sound on a worn tape | [`worn`](../examples/worn.cells) | A flute recorded onto a worn tape loop and played back by two heads, one of them wandering. | 10 | 0:10 loop |

### Tier 9 · Gates, performing and MIDI

Introduces a gate: a product with a name; a braid left to the performer, recorded from the keys; a MIDI card, its entries channels.

| piece | file | about | postgain | length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A gate: a product with a name | [`gate`](../examples/gate.cells) | Where notes become sound, named: a gate plays its voices with each note of what it plays. | 1 | 0:05 loop |
| Play in: a braid left to the performer | [`play-in`](../examples/play-in.cells) | A riff left to the performer: free(…) around a braid. It plays as written until you play in. | 2.51 | 0:03 loop |
| MIDI out: a band on a synth | [`midi-out`](../examples/midi-out.cells) | The piece names where its notes go: a melody and a bass on a synth's channels 1 and 2, the drums on 10. The bass is sent, not heard. | .891 | 0:05 loop |
